# CG-RES-019: Non-success response added

A new non-success response was documented.

**Why it matters:** Documenting an error response does not change what consumers already handle.

| Attribute | Value |
|---|---|
| Area | [Responses](./#res) |
| Detects | `response.added` |
| Severity | breaking: high · potentially breaking: low · undetermined: low |
| Classification can be overridden | no (the rule only fires when the change is breaking by definition) |

## Message

> Response {status} is now documented for {operation}.
>
> Its schema is compared against what the previous fallback response documented.
>
> **Fix:** No action needed.

## Examples

Each example is an executed test case of the rule (`packages/engine/test/compat/fixtures.ts`).

### Fires: 429 added

```diff
  openapi: 3.1.0
  info: {title: t, version: v}
  paths:
    /x:
      get:
-       responses: {'200': {description: ok}}
+       responses: {'200': {description: ok}, '429': {description: slow}}
```

**Result:** Non-breaking, info. Response 429 is now documented for GET /x.

### Fires: strictResponseValidation

With options: `{"policy":{"strictResponseValidation":true,"constraintTightening":"potentially-breaking","responseEnumAdditions":"potentially-breaking","removedRequestParameters":"non-breaking","closedResponseAdditions":"potentially-breaking"}}`

```diff
  openapi: 3.1.0
  info: {title: t, version: v}
  paths:
    /x:
      get:
-       responses: {'200': {description: ok}}
+       responses: {'200': {description: ok}, '429': {description: slow}}
```

**Result:** Potentially breaking, low. Response 429 is now documented for GET /x.

### Does not fire: success response added

```diff
  openapi: 3.1.0
  info: {title: t, version: v}
  paths:
    /x:
      get:
-       responses: {'200': {description: ok}}
+       responses: {'200': {description: ok}, '201': {description: ok}}
```

**Result:** no finding from this rule.
